messages:
PagerDuty Bot: HIGH: gpu-pool-aws-us-west-2 queue length > 1200 for 2m, latency SLO violations on /v1/generate — paging oncall. Pager: Kyle (oncall)
Kyle (oncall): acked, incoming. pulling up pool dashboard and autoscaler logs.
Kyle (oncall): seeing continuous queue growth on us-west-2-gpu-pool, pending pods stuck in Provisioning for >3m. autoscaler events show 'QuotaExceeded' from cloud provider.
Sanjay Patel: joining, oncall handover here. Which customers are impacted?
Alice Martinez: we have increased 5xx rates for dedicated customers in us-west-2 (customers: acme-app, beta-inc). Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example/dashboards/allocations/us-west-2 (shared)
Jessica Wu: can we route new requests to fallback region (us-east-1) temporarily? what's current headroom there?
DevOps Bot: Routing policy note: canary fallback to us-east-1 is enabled for 'hosted' tier but not for 'dedicated' by default. Need manual override or emergency policy.
Sanjay Patel: ok start manual routing override for hosted traffic now. Alice, are the 5xx errors from hosted or dedicated?
Alice Martinez: mix — hosted latency spikes for new sessions, dedicated customers hitting capacity (queueing leading to 503). most customer-affecting errors are from dedicated pools.
Kyle (oncall): running aws cli to check quotas: ```aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A``` shows GPU instance limit at account level is at max. provisioning requests return InsufficientInstanceCapacity/QuotaExceeded.
Tom Reynolds: I'm taking lead on contacting AWS support. opening a support case now with priority P1 referencing capacity and quota. Case: 0123456789. Noted ETA unknown.
Dev Support (AWS): (via support channel) we see high regional demand in us-west-2; can request quota increase, typical review 1-4h. For immediate relief consider launching other instance families or alternate AZs.
Sanjay Patel: options: 1) route hosted traffic to us-east-1 (done) 2) for dedicated customers, spin up smaller-instance GPU types (if compatible) 3) enable preemptible spot GPUs in other regions 4) ask customers to temporarily reduce QPS (notify). Which is fastest?
Jessica Wu: fastest is routing hosted -> us-east-1 (already toggled). For dedicated, enabling spot fallback and spinning different instance types is next — need config patch to allow g4dn fallback.
Kyle (oncall): applying patch to autoscaler profile to accept g4dn-family and spot capacity as fallback. Pushing change: ```kubectl apply -f autoscaler/fallback-g4dn.yaml```
DevOps Bot: deploy bot: autoscaler config updated in us-west-2 — new fallback families added. Note: instance type mismatch may require model kernel fallback; performance will be degraded.
Alice Martinez: I see a small drop in queued requests (~10%) but dedicated customers still showing high tail latency. Errors down from 8% -> 4% for hosted.
Tom Reynolds: update from AWS support: quota request submitted for GPU instances, sent to regional team for expedited review. No immediate guarantee.
Sanjay Patel: initiating customer communication draft for impacted customers: short note about degraded performance and mitigation steps. Alice please coordinate.
Alice Martinez: drafted message in #customer-updates, requesting approval. Will send with 'partial degradation, fallback active' phrasing.
Jessica Wu: we should also enable aggressive batching reduction to lower memory pressure and reduce pending pods. Patch: reduce max_tokens_per_request and enable dynamic batching threshold. Applying now.
Kyle (oncall): applied batching config: ```POST /api/configs/autoscale -d '{"dynamic_batch_ms":50,"max_batch_tokens":1024}'``` — rolling out to runtime.
DevOps Bot: runtime config updated across us-west-2 nodes. Observability: token cost per request decreased; queue growth plateauing.
Sanjay Patel: timeline update for incident channel: cause = regional GPU quota/capacity exhaustion in AWS us-west-2 causing autoscaler to stall (QuotaExceeded). Mitigations = hosted traffic routed to us-east-1, autoscaler fallback to alternate instance families + spot, batching reduction. Customer impact = elevated latency and 503s for some dedicated customers for ~20-40 minutes.
Tom Reynolds: AWS case updated with these mitigations, asking for quota bump and region-level capacity confirmation.
Dev Support (AWS): acknowledged, escalated to regional capacity team. We'll post updates in the support case.
Alice Martinez: sending customer e-mail now. :email:
Jessica Wu: monitoring — queue now decreasing, tail latency for hosted mostly recovered; dedicated still catching up, but error rate trending down to <1.5%.
Kyle (oncall): recording timeline and actions in postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/2234567890-usw2-quotahit (saving notes).
Sanjay Patel: will remain on call for next 30m for handoff. If AWS confirms quota increase, we'll revert fallback routing and restore original autoscaler families only after steady-state for 15m.
Tom Reynolds: thanks all — great rapid coordination. :thumbsup:
PagerDuty Bot: RESOLVED alert: gpu-pool-aws-us-west-2 queue length returned below threshold for 10m.
Kyle (oncall): marking incident as mitigated, leaving notes for SRE postmortem and action items: request permanent quota increase, enable pre-approved emergency routing for dedicated customers, add runbook step to add fallback families via a single toggle.
Sanjay Patel: assigning owners: quotas (Tom), routing runbook (Jessica), customer comms follow-up (Alice). Closing thread after postmortem update.
